bull_bear.body:
- Over thirty years of expertise in the engineering and construction sector, offering comprehensive EPC solutions
- Proven track record of delivering projects across diverse sectors including Power, Oil and Gas, Roads, Railways and Metros, Water and Irrigation, Ports, and Buildings & Structures
- Proficiency across various infrastructure domains supported by a skilled workforce
- Successful completion of several projects of national importance despite severe challenges
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Unresolved IL&FS resolution process and 'Red Entity' classification — Under the IL&FS resolution framework the Company is classified as a 'Red Entity', indicating its current inability to service debt and operational liabilities. The NCLAT moratorium covers all liabilities existing as on the 15 October 2018 cut-off date, so the Company is not servicing pre-cut-off dues to lenders and operational creditors. The resolution process is still underway, has a significant impact on business plans, and business realignment and financial restructuring are expected to continue over the next several months with significant uncertainties.
- Fully eroded net worth constraining bank guarantees and new bidding — The Company's net worth is fully eroded and prevailing financial constraints, particularly on bank guarantee requirements, have currently limited its ability to participate in new project bidding despite substantial prospects across Power, Oil & Gas, Railways & Metros, Roads and Buildings & Structures. The Company also continues to default on loans to lenders including borrowings from promoter group entities.
- Order book risk - prolonged absence of new order inflows — The Company has experienced a prolonged period of limited order inflows over the past six years, except for two subcontracting assignments (Surat Metro Rail Works for Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation and Bhubaneswar Metro Rail Works for Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, the latter shelved by the Govt. of Odisha). Existing projects are nearing completion or approaching end of term, which has already caused a significant reduction in operations over the past three years.
- Reputation and brand risk from the IL&FS group debt crisis — The IL&FS Group debt crisis and related corporate governance concerns have adversely impacted the reputation of associated entities including the Company, creating challenges in securing new EPC contracts, obtaining favourable financing and availing credit support from vendors and suppliers.
- Operational / project execution risk — Operational challenges in project execution may result in cost escalations and schedule overruns; mitigation rests on detailed planning and control over project design, subcontractor selection, supplier management, recruitment, resource deployment and insurance, supported by documented SOPs and project monitoring systems.
- Subcontractor and joint venture dependence — Dependence on subcontractors and joint venture partners for project execution exposes the Company to non-performance risk that may adversely impact revenue and profitability; mitigated through stringent evaluation and selection and continuous performance monitoring.
- Contractual and claims/arbitration risk — The Company is exposed to contractual risk in dealings with clients, subcontractors, suppliers and lenders in the ordinary course of business; a dedicated Contracts Department handles contract administration, management of significant claims and coordination of arbitration proceedings with the Legal team.
- Material risk - surplus stock at completed, foreclosed or terminated sites — Materials lying at completed, foreclosed or terminated project sites cannot be redeployed given the inability to secure new projects; the Company is undertaking disposal of surplus materials, subject to necessary approvals, to minimise losses from deterioration, obsolescence or theft.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company offers comprehensive Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) solutions and has been predominantly engaged in executing infrastructure projects throughout India, leveraging proficiency across various infrastructure domains and a skilled workforce. It has a track record of delivering projects across Power, Oil and Gas, Roads, Railways and Metros, Water and Irrigation, Ports, and Buildings & Structures. It is currently executing EPC and item-rate projects for both government and private clients, most of which are nearing completion, while it awaits resolution as part of the IL&FS group.

outlook.body: - Management frames the Company's forthcoming opportunity set around the infrastructure verticals it already operates in - Roads, Railways & Metros, Water & Irrigation, Oil & Gas, Ports, Airports and Power & Renewable Energy ('The forthcoming opportunities in the business sectors of IECCL are as follows').
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections disclose no capex, capacity-addition or expansion programme of the Company itself. The Directors' Report records no change in the nature of business during the year, that there was no change in share capital, that no amount was transferred to Reserves, and that the Company continues to default on existing loans to lenders including borrowings from promoters while following the terms of the moratorium of the Hon'ble NCLAT, Mumbai; the Company remains part of the IL&FS group awaiting resolution under the NCLAT-approved framework, with the plan under consideration by Hon'ble Justice D K Jain (Retd.) ahead of sanction by the Hon'ble NCLT, Mumbai. The expansion narrative in the MD&A is entirely third-party - the government and industry pipeline that frames the addressable opportunity for the Company's EPC business: Bharatmala Phase I developing 34,800 km of national highways slated for completion by 2027-2028 plus 22 new Greenfield expressways and 35 Multimodal Logistics Parks; a 13,400 km three-year PPP road pipeline and a ~10,000 km highway construction target for FY 2026-27; seven proposed high-speed rail corridors (Mumbai-Pune, Pune-Hyderabad, Hyderabad-Bangalore, Hyderabad-Chennai, Chennai-Bangalore, Delhi-Varanasi and Varanasi-Siliguri), metro/MRTS funding, 15,000 km of automatic signalling and 37,000 km of KAVACH fitment, and a new Dankuni-Surat dedicated freight corridor; the Jal Jeevan Mission extended till 2028 for 100 percent rural piped water coverage and a Rs 25,000 crore Maritime Development Fund; port, waterway and container-manufacturing initiatives including 20 new National Waterways and the National Maritime Heritage Complex at Lothal; airport capital outlay of about Rs 98,000 crore over five years and 15 airport projects worth US$ 12.1 billion by 2028; and in power and renewables a 500 GW renewable target, 81 thermal units identified to be replaced by renewable generation by 2028, roughly 170 GW of installed renewable capacity expected by March 2026, a Rs 20,000 crore CCUS outlay and Rs 9,12,000 crore of planned power transmission investment by 2032.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India is expected to be one of the top three economic powers in the world over the next 10-15 years; the economy is projected to grow by 7.4% in 2026, with the IMF raising its fiscal 2026 growth forecast to 7.3% from a previous-year 6.5%.
- Capital expenditure on infrastructure development is expected to have strong multiplier effects on growth in the coming years, with the public sector continuing to play a pivotal role in funding large-scale infrastructure, physical and digital connectivity and social infrastructure.
- Union Budget 2026-27 re-emphasises Viksit Bharat 2047 and infrastructure development; public capital expenditure is proposed to rise about 9% to Rs 12.2 lakh crore in FY 2026-27 from Rs 11.21 lakh crore, supporting crowding-in of private investment.
- A new Asset Monetization Plan and a three-year PPP project pipeline are expected to encourage private sector engagement; asset monetisation for 2026-30 is to plough back Rs 10 lakh crore of capital into new projects.
- The India Infrastructure Sector Market is expected to reach USD 205.96 billion in 2026, growing at a CAGR of 9.57% over the forecast period.
- Roads: the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has been allocated Rs 3,09,875 crore, with a FY 2026-27 highway construction target of about 10,000 km, a 13,400 km three-year PPP pipeline and Bharatmala Phase I targeting 34,800 km of national highways by 2027-2028.
- Railways and metros: a record Rs 2,93,030 crore allocation for Indian Railways, seven proposed high-speed rail corridors, substantial urban metro/MRTS funding, KAVACH and automatic-signalling rollouts, and a new Dankuni-Surat dedicated freight corridor.
- Water and irrigation: extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission till 2028 targeting 100 percent coverage of rural piped water supply, with continued allocations for water and sanitation infrastructure.
- Ports and maritime: a Rs 25,000 crore Maritime Development Fund, 20 new National Waterways planned, and a target to double inland waterways and coastal shipping freight share from 6% to 12% by 2047.
- Oil & gas: Rs 30,443 crore allocation to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, refining capacity expected to reach 300 MTPA by 2028 and 100% FDI allowed in upstream and private-sector refining projects.
- Airports: a targeted capital outlay of about Rs 98,000 crore by AAI and other airport developers over the next five years, and 15 airport projects worth US$ 12.1 billion by 2028.
- Power and renewables: an investment opportunity worth Rs 40,00,000 crore over the next decade, a 39% higher Ministry of Power allocation with 60% directed to the RDSS, a 500 GW renewable energy target, MNRE allocation up 30%, and Rs 9,12,000 crore planned for power transmission by 2032.

deepdive.thesis: IL&FS Engineering and Construction Company Limited (IECCL) is an India-focused engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor with over thirty years of experience across infrastructure sectors, currently operating under the IL&FS group resolution framework.

open.item: The bid-cum-resolution plan, already approved by the secured lenders, is to be cleared by Hon'ble Justice D K Jain (Retd.) and then sanctioned by the Hon'ble NCLT, Mumbai, following which admitted unsecured operational-creditor claims as on the 15 October 2018 cut-off date will be settled.
All efforts are directed towards completing the order book in hand and liaising with clients for financial closure of completed projects and projects where amicable foreclosures have been signed.

The Company is awaiting resolution under the framework approved by the Hon'ble NCLAT, Delhi, with the resolution process under consideration for approval by Hon'ble Justice D K Jain (Retd.), after which approval of the Hon'ble NCLT, Mumbai, is to be obtained as a pre-requisite for resolution of the Company.

litigation.note: The Company is part of the IL&FS group and its resolution process, initiated by the reconstituted IL&FS Board under orders of the Hon'ble NCLAT, is still underway. A binding bid received from an overseas Fund for the promoters' equity stake has been approved by the secured lenders with an overwhelming majority; the bid-cum-resolution plan is under consideration by Hon'ble Justice D K Jain (Retd.) and would be followed by sanction of the Hon'ble NCLT, Mumbai. Under the plan, unsecured dues of operational creditors as on the 15 October 2018 cut-off date, as admitted by the Claim Advisor, would be settled, and legal cases filed against the Company pertaining to pre-October 2018 claims are stated to stand infructuous. The Directors' Report records that no new significant or material orders have been passed by regulators, courts or tribunals impacting the going concern status.
